
Functions that work along an axis typically allow you to provide it by position
or by title.

# Positions

A position counts axes from `1`. Axis `1` runs down the rows, axis `2` runs
across the columns, and so on.

```{r}
x <- array(
  1:24,
  dim = c(2, 3, 4),
  dimnames = list(row = NULL, col = NULL, page = NULL)
)

rray_dimensions(rray_sum(x, axes = 1))
```

# Titles

Titles are the names of the dimension names list, like `row` in
`list(row = NULL)`. [rray_titles()] returns them. A title works most anywhere a
position does:

```{r}
rray_titles(x)

identical(rray_sum(x, axes = "row"), rray_sum(x, axes = 1))

identical(rray_sum(x, axes = c("page", "row")), rray_sum(x, axes = c(1, 3)))
```

# Positions in the output

Some arguments specify a position in the output rather than an axis of `x`,
like `axes` in [rray_insert_axes()] and `.axis` in [rray_stack()]. That axis
doesn't exist yet, so it has no title, and these arguments only take positions:

```{r, error = TRUE}
rray_dimensions(rray_insert_axes(x, axes = 1))

rray_insert_axes(x, axes = "row")
```
